headline: Wednesday morning front: the latest HRRR cut its burst by roughly two-thirds, but the other models still show a soaking burst late morning.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A deepening low off the Pacific Northwest drags a strong cold front through the Bay Area Wednesday morning. NWS San Francisco expects rain to pick up 4–8 AM in the North Bay and sweep across the Peninsula roughly 6–10 AM, with isolated thunderstorms possible along the front. Showers and a better chance of thunderstorms follow Wednesday night into Thursday morning as colder air and a surface low move in. NWS storm totals through Friday morning: 1.5–2.5 in for most of the Bay Area. Another, weaker front arrives Saturday.

sections.title: Model trends
sections.text: The headline change this afternoon is the HRRR. Its midday run had close to 0.9 in in a single hour around 7–8 AM and about 1.4 in for the wettest 3 hours, which would have matched our worst floods. The 2 PM run shows only about 0.2 in in the wettest hour and about 0.4 in for the wettest 3 hours (8–11 AM). The other models did not follow it down. RRFS (10 AM run) still has about 0.65 in in one hour around 11 AM and 1.1 in in 3 hours; the NWS blend (NBM) has about 0.9 in and ECMWF about 0.8 in. Storm totals through Thursday run about 2.5–3.1 in in RRFS, NBM and ECMWF, while HRRR's total is about 1.4 in (to the end of its run). When one model swings this much between runs and the others don't, the safer read is that the timing and placement of the frontal band are uncertain, not that the storm has gone away. The next HRRR runs tonight should show whether the drop holds.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text: Redwood City high tide is predicted at 7.0 ft (MLLW) at 7:21 AM Wednesday, and NOAA's Bay model adds about 1.5 ft of surge (near 8.6 ft). NWS has a Coastal Flood Advisory from 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM Thursday. The Bay can't reach the street directly, but a high Bay keeps the Bayfront Canal and Atherton Channel from draining, so the channel can't take water as fast while the heaviest rain may be falling. That overlap is the setup to watch. Thursday's high is a bit higher (7.4 ft predicted at 7:58 AM), in case the Thursday-morning thunderstorms deliver a second burst.

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry this evening. Atherton Channel at Caltrain is essentially empty, so the system starts with all of its capacity. The ground is damp from Sunday and Monday's rain, so runoff will come quickly.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Model spread is large: 0.4 to 1.1 in for the wettest 3 hours. Frontal rain bands are narrow, so a 10–20 mile shift decides whether the heaviest core passes over Atherton. HRRR has under-forecast every big local burst in our records, by about 3× in the worst cases (Mar 2023, Dec 2025), and any thunderstorm along the front can drop 0.5 in in 20–30 minutes. Timing is uncertain by about ±2 hours. Most likely outcome: Green to Yellow at the peak. Red needs about 1.2 in in 3 hours, which only RRFS comes close to. Purple is not supported by any model.

sections.title: What to do tonight
sections.text:
• Move cars out of the cul-de-sac before about 7 AM.
• Clear leaves from the street drain grates and yard drains this evening. The first big wind of the season brings down leaves, and a clogged grate floods the street at much lower rain totals.
• If you use sandbags, set them before bed; the heaviest rain could start soon after daylight.
• Wind Advisory overnight: power outages are possible. The pump station needs power; if the power goes out during heavy rain, assume the pumps may be slow and watch the street.
• During the peak, take a photo of the street with the time visible. Every documented storm improves the warning levels.
• Keep the dashboard open in a tab: the 1-hour burst alarm needs live readings.
• Don't drive or walk through moving water.

summary.text: Big drop: HRRR's wettest 3 hours fell from about 1.4 in (midday run) to about 0.4 in (2 PM run). That alone would mean only Blue–Green.
Models disagree: RRFS 1.1 in, NBM 0.9, ECMWF 0.8 for the wettest 3 hours. HRRR is now the low outlier, and it has under-forecast big bursts here before.
Most likely Green to Yellow (water toward the garage doors) at the peak. Red is unlikely unless a thunderstorm cell sits over the area.
NWS has the front crossing the Bay Area 6–10 AM Wednesday; models put the heaviest hour 8–11 AM. Showers and thunderstorms return Wednesday night into Thursday.
7.0 ft high tide at 7:21 AM plus ~1.5 ft surge (Coastal Flood Advisory). The channel drains slowly through mid-morning, right before the rain peaks. Channel is empty now.
Cars out of the cul-de-sac before 7 AM; clear street drain grates tonight. Watch the 1-hour burst alarm on the dashboard.
